title: Rankings, ADP and Auction Prices: What to Trust in a 9-Cat League
brief: Why are Yahoo ranks, X-rank, ADP and straight 9-cat total rankings unreliable for our H2H 9-cat league, and how do points-league values leak into our draft room? It must show how to use rank versus market price to find value and when a gap between sites is an opportunity.
summary: No single public list tells you what a player is worth in our 12-team H2H 9-cat auction. Yahoo ranks, X-rank and ADP blend points and category drafts, and straight 9-cat totals inflate some players and sink others. Treat ranks and ADP as the market's price, use a format-matched H2H ranking as your value, and only act on gaps of 15 to 20 spots or more.

sections.heading: Every number needs a format attached

paragraphs.text: A ranking means nothing unless you know which format it was built for. Value differs between H2H categories, roto, Yahoo points, ESPN points and Sleeper. Labels like sleeper, bust or overrated are also empty without a format. Our league is H2H, 9 categories, 12 teams, with turnovers counted. Before you trust a list, check that it matches all of that.

Yahoo X-rank is a vibes-based expert list. It ignores your league format and often sits somewhere between points value and category value. Our draft room will sort by X-rank by default. Before 2026-10-18, re-sort your queue so it does not follow X-rank, and load your own H2H 9-cat values instead.

The experts disagree on whether Yahoo's other rank column adjusts to your league. One note says the separate 'rank' column comes from statistical projections and changes with league settings. Other notes say Yahoo ranks and ADPs are the same for every format and do not change with your settings. Another says Yahoo ranks some players for category leagues and others for points leagues. The safe approach: assume no Yahoo number is built for H2H 9-cat until you have checked it against a ranking you know is format-matched.

sections.heading: Why straight 9-cat totals mislead in H2H

paragraphs.text: Several experts refuse to use straight 9-cat rankings at all. One calls ranking by 9-cat totals the worst way to rank players. Another says that if a player needs a 50-spot adjustment to reflect his real value, the system is broken. If you lean on one of these lists, you must accept every result it gives. One per-game list put Giannis around 69th or 70th. If you do not believe that, do not use the list for anyone else either.

The main problem is '9-cat fluff'. The traditional Z-score method includes turnovers and overrates players who are strong in only a few categories. In H2H you want to max out games played, so low turnovers matter less than the formula says. Box-score values also overrate blocks, steals and some percentages. One H2H system pushes centers down for this reason. Fluffed players get overdrafted, so expect someone in our room to pay for them.

The error runs both ways. A low 9-cat rank can make a useful player look like a bench or waiver player. Paolo Banchero is the example given. On the other side, one note calls Turner's top-20 finish a flaw in the rankings, and says Zubac's 9-cat rank did not reflect his real value. Full-season totals add another bias. A player who played a lot of games, such as Reed Sheppard with 82, gets ranked far too high.

Punt-adjusted lists create a related trap. A one-category specialist can look like a top-100 player once you punt his weak categories. That does not make him draftable in a standard league. With 144 players drafted, only pay for a specialist if you are actually building the punt that suits him.

sections.heading: How points-league value leaks into our draft room

paragraphs.text: Yahoo is the most-used platform, and its rankings drive ADP in mocks and real drafts. Yahoo ranks are format agnostic, and ADP tends to follow them. Yahoo ADP also mixes points drafts with category drafts. That is how points-league favourites end up high in a 9-cat room and at the top of autodraft queues. Any manager who auto-bids or follows the default list will carry that points bias into our auction.

Know the profile that leaks in. High-usage, volume scorers with weak defensive stats and lower efficiency are worth more in points leagues. Usage tracks points-league value closely but tracks category success much less. One such scorer can be top 10 in points leagues and only a third-rounder in categories. Do not pay early-round money for a player whose value is mostly points. In 9-cat, efficiency, assists, steals and blocks matter more.

The leak also creates discounts. A player can be a fair pick at a given spot in points leagues but too early in category leagues, and the reverse is true. When the site ranks or drafts a player for the other format, he can be mispriced. In our league, look for players whose ADP leans toward a weaker points value. Their category value has not been priced in yet.
Many drafters do not know why a player is ranked where he is, so bad ranks fool a lot of people. That is your edge. Many prices in a room are too high or too low only because of the format.

sections.heading: Rank versus price: using the gap

paragraphs.text: Keep two numbers apart. Your format-matched ranking measures a player's quality. ADP and Yahoo rank are the market price and tell you when he will likely be taken. The example rule: if you rank a player 30th and his ADP is 70th, take him in the 50s. Do not pay your full value when the room will let you pay less. In our auction, that means bidding above where the market prices him, but stopping well short of your own value until the room shows it disagrees.

Only act on large gaps. A gap of a few spots leaves no margin for error. A gap of 15 to 20 spots between ADP and your expected value still protects you if the player underperforms. Treat smaller gaps as noise.

ADP is an average, not a median. A player with ADP 50 goes after pick 50 in roughly half of drafts, so he often goes earlier than the number suggests. An ADP of 46 means he goes outside the top 50 in some leagues. Do not assume a player will last to his ADP. If you need him, nominate or bid before his average spot.

Our draft is an auction, and Yahoo auction price data has differed a lot from snake ADP. Treat the two separately. Use auction values to plan your 200 USD budget and use ADP only as a rough guide to demand. Rank and ADP matter in different ways from league to league. Some leagues follow ranks, some follow ADP, and some go rogue. In the early nominations, watch which pattern our room follows and adjust.

sections.heading: When a gap between sites is an opportunity

paragraphs.text: Rankings differ a lot between Yahoo, ESPN and Fantrax, so whether a player is a bust or a steal depends on platform and format. Learn how each site presents its data. You gain value from the gaps. Convert ESPN ranks before comparing. ESPN's default leagues use 10 teams and 8 categories. We play 12 teams and 9 categories with turnovers.

A real opportunity looks like this. A player's ESPN ADP sits far later than his rank, which means drafters keep passing on him. If he also ranks well on your H2H list, target him. A second signal is two players with similar category profiles, such as rebounds, blocks and FG%, who sit far apart in ADP. That gap is a market inefficiency. Buy the cheaper one.

Some gaps are fake. Ignore a Yahoo ADP built on very few drafts, because it can be inflated. Ignore ADPs distorted by dynasty leagues where the player is drafted in only a small share of leagues. Remember that ADPs tend to follow last season, so a gap may only reflect old results. Rank and ADP also move together. When Yahoo moves a rank back, the ADP drifts later too.

ADPs are not set by a person. They update every day from real drafts, so no site will 'fix' a number you think is wrong. Today is 2026-10-11 and our draft is 2026-10-18. Recheck your gap list on draft day, because the numbers in the room will be the current ones.
